pages.lesson:
LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 6.1.1 SELF-EXPRESSION – INTERVIEWS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 6.1: Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Self-expression – interviews

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! Today we learn about Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Self-expression – interviews. Read the explanation, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

Big question: How do we listen to get information from an aural text?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify gender roles from aural texts for information
2. respond to questions on gender roles in the community from texts for comprehension

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

• Listening and Speaking 6.1.1 Self-expression – interviews helps you communicate well at school and at home.

• Listen with your eyes and ears. Face the speaker and wait for your turn.

• When you speak, use a clear voice and polite words.

• Practise short dialogues with a partner using Kenyan school situations.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: When you meet your teacher in the morning, say “Good morning” clearly and smile.

Example 2: Listen to a short instruction, then repeat it to a friend in your own words.

Example 3: Role-play buying an item at the market using polite requests: “Please…”, “Thank you.”

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Practise a 30-second greeting dialogue with a partner.
2. Listen to three instructions and carry them out in order.
3. Tell a short news item from your day using complete sentences.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Teach a younger learner one polite greeting from this lesson.
2. Write five sentences you can say when welcoming a visitor at school.
3. Ask a parent to give you three oral instructions; write them down after listening.

SECTION 7: CLASS ACTIVITY IDEAS

1. Listen to a recording or talk on the theme,
2. Prepare a vocabulary list with the words related to the theme,
3. Make simple sentences using the vocabulary identified,
4. Work collaboratively to conduct 1. How do we listen to get information from an aural text? 2. Why should some opportunities be equal among both girls and boys? 2 a debate on the theme - gender roles,
5. Digital Literacy: This is enhanced as the learner uses digital technology to accomplish tasks when teaming up with peers to record the debate session.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we listen to get information from an aural text?
2. Why should some opportunities be equal among both girls and boys?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Good listeners look, wait, and respond.
2. Clear speech helps others understand you.
3. Polite language shows respect.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original learner lesson from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
